title: CWE-942: CORS allow_credentials=True with wildcard methods/headers and hardcoded origins
description: main.py:13-19 configures CORSMiddleware with allow_credentials=True, allow_methods=['*'], allow_headers=['*'] and allow_origins=settings.CORS_ORIGINS (localhost:3000, localhost:5173, https://dfcont.com.br, hardcoded in config.py:17-21). With credentials enabled, any origin that is or becomes allowlisted can read credentialed responses; the methods/headers wildcards maximize what a compromised/evil page on an allowlisted origin can request. The localhost origins are dev-only and should not exist in a production allowlist; the real deployed origin list is unverified. CORS is defense-in-depth only (server has no auth), but the combination is fragile against allowlist drift.
impact: Credential-bearing cross-origin requests permitted broadly; if an attacker ever controls content on an allowlisted origin (or the allowlist drifts), credentialed data and state-changing calls become reachable from the browser.
mitigation: Restrict methods/headers to the concrete verbs and headers used; remove localhost origins from the production allowlist; document the exact production origin(s); if credentials are not actually needed, set allow_credentials=False.
